title: Fine-tuning an ECG Foundation Model to Predict Coronary CT Angiography Outcomes
abstract: arXiv:2512.05136v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a major global public health burden, yet scalable pre-imaging risk stratification tools are limited. In this multicenter study, we developed and validated an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) model using coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) as the anatomical reference to predict vessel-specific hemodynamically significant stenosis ($\geq 70\%$ for RCA, LAD, LCX; $\geq 50\%$ for LM). The model was evaluated in internal and external cohorts, clinically normal ECGs, and prespecified demographic and clinical subgroups. It showed discrimination across vessels in internal validation and consistent external and normal ECG performance. Predicted probabilities increased with CCTA-defined stenosis severity and were converted into vessel-specific low-, intermediate-, and high-risk strata. Calibration and decision curve analyses supported its clinical utility. Int

translated_title: 微调心电图基础模型以预测冠状动脉CT血管造影结果
translated_abstract: 冠状动脉疾病（CAD）仍然是全球主要的公共卫生负担，但可扩展的影像前风险分层工具有限。在这项多中心研究中，我们开发并验证了一种人工智能心电图（AI-ECG）模型，使用冠状动脉计算机断层血管造影（CCTA）作为解剖参考，以预测血管特异性的血流动力学显著狭窄（右冠状动脉、左前降支、左旋支≥70%；左主干≥50%）。该模型在内部和外部队列、临床正常心电图以及预设的人口统计学和临床亚组中进行了评估。它在内部验证中显示出跨血管的区分能力，并在外部和正常心电图性能上表现一致。预测概率随CCTA定义的狭窄严重程度增加而增加，并被转换为血管特异性的低、中、高风险分层。校准和决策曲线分析支持其临床实用性。
tldr: 本研究通过微调心电图基础模型，利用CCTA作为解剖参考，成功预测了血管特异性的显著冠脉狭窄，并提供了风险分层，增强了临床实用性。
en_tdlr: This study fine-tunes an ECG foundation model to predict vessel-specific significant coronary stenosis using CCTA as reference, enhancing risk stratification and clinical utility.
